market.headline: The AI selloff became a broad flush: QQQ fell 5.7% and SPY fell 3.6% on 2.4x and 2.6x normal volume, and QQQ now sits 20.2% below its 52-week high.
market.day_type: A broad tech-led selloff close to capitulation. The Nvidia scandal deepened, chips were dumped together, the newly listed Anthropic slid, and a 10-year yield of 5.07 plus a VIX of 24.56 left no buyers for expensive growth.
watch: Monday open: QQQ 606.23 is Friday's low. A break means the flush isn't over. A close back above 643.28 is the first sign of a bottom. On SPY the same lines are 686.75 and 715.65.
Mon Nov 23 and Tue Nov 24 (dates estimated): HPE and DELL report. They are the first real read on AI server demand since the rout, with a direct knock-on for SMCI, NVDA and AMD.
Wed Nov 25, 08:30: GDP and PCE inflation. With the 10-year at 5.07, a hot print hits tech again.

stocks.headline: Fell 14.0% to 125.53, a new 52-week low, ending its longest weekly losing streak since 2008. Morning call (don't buy): right.
stocks.why: The business is not the problem. Sales grew 106% last quarter, the operating margin is 65%, forecasts rose 27% in 90 days, and it trades at 9x next year's profit. The problem is legal. California's attorney general subpoenaed the company and said Nvidia may have misled investors, and the former CEO will testify before the Senate about his China ties. That kind of risk does not show up in earnings, so cheapness alone is not a reason to buy. Nvidia leads the whole chip group, so every new headline here also hits AMD, TSM, ARM, MU, AVGO and SMCI.

long_term.reason: This agrees with the house view. The company is cheap and still growing fast, but the subpoena and the Senate hearing are open legal risks to the company itself, not just to its share price.

stocks.what_would_change_it: If the investigation finds misleading statements or brings new China export limits, the stance moves to Avoid. If it closes back above 145.71 after the testimony with no new charges, the stance moves to Add on dips.
stocks.action: Don't buy the after-hours bounce or Monday's open. Buy a first slice only after a daily close back above 145.71.

levels.means: Above = Friday's low is holding for now. Below = a new 52-week low with no support underneath, so stay out.
Above = it has recovered all of Friday's drop and sellers are tiring. Below = still in the selloff.
A close above = first real repair and the buy trigger. Below = keep waiting.

stocks.headline: Fell 13.2% to 424.39 after a short-seller report on China links and news that US-approved chip sales reached groups tied to China's military. Morning call (don't buy the open): right.
stocks.why: The numbers are strong. Profit per share is up 74%, sales are up 45% and speeding up, it has beaten forecasts five quarters running, and it trades at 28x next year's profit. The damage comes from the claim that its firmware turned up at a blacklisted Chinese company. That raises the risk of export curbs or a probe like Nvidia's, and AMD has not answered the claim yet. The stock now sits right on its 200-day average of 429.79. That is the line between a pullback inside an uptrend and a broken trend.

long_term.reason: This agrees with the house view. Growth and forecasts are excellent, but an unanswered China allegation in the middle of the Nvidia scandal is the kind of news that keeps growing before it goes away.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A clear public rebuttal from AMD and a close back above 429.79 make it a Buy. A government probe or new export ban makes it Avoid.
stocks.action: Don't buy Monday. Buy a first slice only if AMD publicly answers the report and the stock then closes above 429.79.

levels.means: Above = the November low still holds. Below = the whole rebound is undone, so stay out.
A close above = the long-term uptrend is intact and you can buy if AMD has answered. Below = the trend is breaking.
Above = Friday's drop has been fully reversed. Below = sellers are still in charge.

stocks.headline: Fell only 2.7% to 265.29, a new 52-week low, while QQQ fell 5.7%. A YouTube settlement over teen addiction claims is reportedly near. Morning call: too early, because it traded above 272.66 and then closed below the 270.0 wait line.
stocks.why: Alphabet held up best of the big tech names. It trades at 14x trailing profit, its lowest in five years, with $567.7B of contracted backlog and $56.3B in cash. The weak spot is real, though. Last quarter it missed forecasts by 30%, profit per share fell 26% while sales grew 25%, and the forward price is higher than the trailing one, so the market expects profits to fall as AI spending rises. The settlement is a one-time cost and does not change the business. Its new teen safeguards are a small drag on YouTube ads.

long_term.reason: This agrees with the house view. You get a cheap, cash-rich company with steady 25% sales growth and a huge backlog. The risk is that spending keeps squeezing profits for another quarter or two.

stocks.what_would_change_it: If profit keeps falling next quarter while capital spending rises again, the stance drops to Hold.
